messages:
Marta Silva: Dropped a compact mock for the escalation timing control — small inline control next to channel pills that lets you set 'wait X minutes before next target'. Uploading PNG.
Jon Erickson: Good. Does X respect route-level overrides and org locks?
Marta Silva: Yes 1 default inherits from route, org-locked values show a lock icon and read-only text.
Priya Menon: Copy nit: label currently 'Delay to next'  propose 'Wait before next attempt' or maybe 'Retry delay'. Which reads better?
Theo Alvarez: 'Retry delay' is concise, 'Wait before next attempt' is clearer for non-SREs. Maybe short label + microcopy.
a11y-bot: Accessibility: the inline control must be keyboard-editable and announce the new value via aria-live. Also ensure the microcopy is linked via aria-describedby.
Jon Erickson: UX: when you change the delay, preview should show simulated timestamps in the preview pane. Don't make users guess.
Marta Silva: I added a small 'simulate' link that plays a 6-step timeline showing timestamps and channel outcomes. It also shows when suppression windows would block retries.
Priya Menon: Microcopy: use 'Applies when previous delivery fails or is unacknowledged' under the control. And define 'unacknowledged' in help text.
Theo Alvarez: For mobile, the control should collapse to a small chevron that opens a spinner-style picker. Keep the pill compact.
Marta Silva: Also adding a tiny cost badge next to SMS with estimated incremental cost for each retry. Tooltip explains assumptions.
a11y-bot: Color guidance: use icon + text, don't rely on red/green. Provide pattern fills in simulation bars for colorblind users.
Jon Erickson: Final thought: track changes to these timing values in audit entries with previous/next values so we can trace alert storms caused by config changes.
Marta Silva: Great. I'll update mocks with locked state, simulation pane timestamps, copy tweaks, cost badge, and a11y notes. Putting artboard in drive: https://drive.redwood/design/escalation-timing-compact
design-bot: Reminder: bring updated artboards to critique tomorrow 9am PT.
Marta Silva: Thanks ":)" — closing thread, drop tiny nits on figma.
